Which department decided that residents cannot return to Wang Fuk Court?

During the question-and-answer session, multiple owners raised this issue. At least five questioners questioned Hop On, asking which department decided that residents cannot currently return to Wang Fuk Court and what was the legal basis for the lockdown. Hop On initially avoided answering directly four times, merely stating that Wang Fuk Court had not yet been unsealed and that it was beyond the manager's authority to arrange, and told owners to contact the dedicated social worker if needed, which at one point caused an uproar among owners at multiple venues.

Hop On unaware of the legal basis for the authorities' lockdown

Solicitor Leung Ping-chiu finally responded, saying that Hop On was unaware of the legal basis on which the authorities imposed the lockdown, and it would be inappropriate to explain on their behalf to avoid misrepresenting the government's considerations. As for the inspection reports for the other seven buildings of Wang Fuk Court, which also drew much attention, Hop On said that the typhoon and rainy seasons were approaching and the reports might be released after the authorities complete their inspections. Hop On also said that after seeking legal advice, it considered the requests to be beyond its responsibilities as manager.

Owners concerned the government is using donations to acquire ownership; will not rebuilding save compensation money for China Taiping?

The government previously stated that it would not rebuild on the original site. At the meeting, many owners were concerned whether this meant the HK$2 billion "fire insurance" calculated based on the cost of restoring the building structure would not be paid out. "Is the government using donations to take back the ownership without rebuilding so as to save compensation money for China Taiping?" Ms Lau, a representative of China Taiping Insurance (Hong Kong), said that once the policy liability is established, the company would pay out according to the policy terms regardless of whether repairs or rebuilding would be carried out, and that the acquisition would not affect the policy liability or the amount of compensation. However, Ms Lau also said that the specific policy and legal liabilities could only be further assessed after the independent committee and relevant government departments completed their investigations and announced the results.

Repair of Wang Chi House estimated at HK$30 million

Hop On also reported on the situation of Wang Chi House, which was unaffected by the fire. Hop On previously stated that repairing Wang Chi House would cost an estimated HK$30 million and take at least nine months, involving re-tiling the external walls and restoring the electrical system, among other works. Today, Hop On updated the total amount to approximately HK$32 million, with a construction period of three to nine months. Solicitor Leung Ping-chiu, invited by Hop On to attend the meeting, pointed out that Wang Chi House is part of the entire estate under the Deed of Mutual Covenant, and to separate it out would require substantial amendments to the DMC with the consent of all owners, a complicated and costly procedure.

Some owners pointed out that Hop On cited the time needed to contact owners as a reason for not convening an owners' meeting before the statutory deadline, yet successfully issued subsidy cheques on behalf of the Urban Renewal Authority earlier this year, questioning: "I'd like to ask what's so difficult, you can't find us owners for a meeting?" Chan Wai-kwong, Hop On's Property Services Director who chaired the meeting, did not respond directly, saying it was a venue issue and that it was indeed difficult to find a venue that could accommodate a thousand residents. In the end, the Home Affairs Department provided a venue, which made the meeting possible. Some owners criticised the explanation as unreasonable: "Hong Kong hosts so many of those mega events and spectacles, easily staging shows for tens of thousands in a single venue, and you tell me you can't find a place for our 2,000 people? That's really hard to accept. I hope you won't use this as an excuse anymore."
